nonPoolDecisions: Reading: all ten questions are required; each printed (a)/(b) part is a 5-mark practice card beside the whole question. Two-point items (“3 mharc+2 mharc”, “An chéad mhír atá ceart = 3 mharc”) are order-dependent (first correct point 3, second 2) and stay whole at 0/3/5; single answers allow 0/5, or 0/3/5 where the scheme prints a 3-mark partial answer. B 5(a) (“Cén dá aidhm …”) prints both aims as one answer at 5 and no split: 0/5.
Reading language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh.” is one deduction from each 50-mark passage total; cards state it without applying it inside a part.

Prescribed prose (2A): (a) prints the prescribed short film Cáca Milis or the prescribed short play An Lasair Choille, each a summary covering five printed points (“Luaigh na pointí seo: (i) … (v)”), which the scheme prices “5 phointe eolais agus 5 mharc ar gach pointe eolais. (5 mharc= 2 mharc ar lomphointe eolais agus 3 mharc ar fhorbairt.)”: under different Atlas headings, a 25-mark card each with every printed point its own 5-mark criterion, and every point is also a practice card. (b) Dís is a 25-mark card (five points at 2 + 3).

Prescribed poetry (3A): each poem is a whole 25-mark card with its printed tariffs ((a) Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní): (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9; (b) An Spailpín Fánach: (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9) and one 0–4 Gaeilge deduction; every printed sub-question is also a practice card. Each poem’s (i) prints four questions (a)–(d) at 2 each: each question is also its own practice card, at 0/2 where the scheme prints only its (2 mharc) and sample answers, and 0/1/2 where it prints a split (Mo ghrá-sa (d) “= 1 mharc + 1 mharc”, An Spailpín Fánach (b) “(1 mharc + 1 mharc)”).

Optional prose (2B) and optional poetry (3B) stay whole: the text is open content chosen by the candidate. 2B(a) is an optional film or an optional play, which the scheme marks alike: one card carrying both printed alternatives (the one-card rule for a film or play under one heading, irish-4-7). 2B(b) is a short story (protagonist 1, five points 22, title and author 2). 3B(a) asks for a modern poem and 3B(b) an old one (“sean-aimseartha”); both file under irish-5-6.
Choice is not a route: Ceist 2 and Ceist 3 are each A or B; each printed question is one card carrying the printed choice and “Freagair (a) agus (b) anseo.”; no combination cards.
Literature language: “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0 – 4 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh.]” is one deduction from each 25-mark question, never inside one sub-question.
caveats: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 reading 100 (A JFK in Éirinn – Caoga Bliain Ó Shin 50, B Fionnuala Britton – Lúthchleasaí Órga na hÉireann 50; ten questions at (a) 5 + (b) 5 each), Ceist 2 prose 50 (A Prós Ainmnithe: (a) Cáca Milis or An Lasair Choille 25 + (b) Dís 25; or B Prós Roghnach: (a) an optional film or play 25 + (b) an optional short story 25), Ceist 3 poetry 50 (A Filíocht Ainmnithe: (a) Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní) 25 + (b) An Spailpín Fánach 25; or B Filíocht Roghnach: (a) a modern poem 25 + (b) an old poem 25).

Printed literature asks: 31 (2A(a) five points for each of two texts 10, 2A(b) 1, 2B(a) 1, 2B(b) 1, each 3A poem’s (i)(a)–(d), (ii) and (iii) 12, 3B(a) and 3B(b) three each 6). The lane’s text-layer counter reads 29: it nests each poem’s (i)(b)–(d) a level above (i)(a), so it counts (d), which the next sub-question follows, as a parent and misses it twice.
The scheme draws its bullets with the SymbolMT glyph the text layer returns as the private-use U+F0B7 (PDF 15–20); the builder reads each span with its font and maps only that reviewed glyph to •.

The scheme’s text layer stores ten boxed headings with the page body (“Páipéar II (200 marc)”, “CEIST 1 (A + B) - LÉAMHTHUISCINT - 100 marc”, “A (50 marc)”, “B (50 marc)”, the CEIST 2/3 and section boxes, 2B’s printed as “B PRÓS ROGHNACH (50 marc)”); the builder removes those exact strings (count pinned).

2013 prints no note above the reading questions; each part prints its own prices and splits (“3 mharc+2 mharc”, “An chéad mhír atá ceart = 3 mharc”). Each passage closes with “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 …]” and the penalty note (“Nóta: Gearrfar pionós i ngeall ar iomarcaíocht. … Taispeánfar go soiléir …”); the last part’s key ends before them.

Paper misprint, noted by the scheme: Reading A Alt 3 prints “Bualadh a bhád patróil” for “Buaileadh”; the scheme’s note under A 3(a) (“Nóta: De bharr earráide ar an scrúdpháipéar, glac leis an leagan mícheart “bualadh” …”) is carried as that criterion’s second guidance line. The card shows the paper as printed.

Reading answers include 3-mark partial answers (A 5(a), B 1(a) “Rás = 3 mharc”, B 3(a), B 4(a)), lists of accepted points under “Dhá fháth as na cinn seo a leanas: 3 mharc+2 mharc = 5 mharc” (A 3(b)), “Dhá phíosa eolais: 3 mharc+2 mharc” (B 1(b)) and “Dhá rud as na roghanna seo a leanas: 3 mharc+2 mharc” (B 3(b)), and A 4(b)’s two lists, a thing he did at 3 and a thing he failed to do at 2, with “An chéad mhír atá ceart = 3 mharc”.

Cáca Milis and An Lasair Choille (2A(a)): the scheme reprints each text’s five printed points and prices the answer once, “5 phointe eolais agus 5 mharc ar gach pointe eolais.”, the split printed “(5 mharc= 2 mharc …)” under the film and “( 5 mharc= 2 mharc …)” under the play, with no sample answers; it does not tie a numbered point to a numbered price, so each printed point taken as one of the five points of information is the reading the cards make (as 2014 Hurlamaboc).
Dís (2A(b)) prints a quotation with its source word (“Dís”, set at the right) before the question; the card keeps both as printed. The scheme prices it as the 2A(a) texts, with no sample points.

2B(a): the scheme marks the optional film and the optional play alike, “5 phointe eolais ag teastáil (5 mharc an ceann ar an gcéad trí phointe eolais+ 4 mharc an ceann ar an dá phointe eolais eile)” (23) and title 1 + writer 1 (“Teideal an scannáin = 1 mharc Ainm an scríbhneora = 1 mharc”, “Teideal an dráma = 1 mharc Ainm an údair = 1 mharc”): one card, the points’ tariff lifted once (the same printed words under each), both title lines lifted. The film’s title line drops its full stop in the scheme (“… a scríobh síos go soiléir Teideal an scannáin”).

2B(b) prices “An príomhcharachtar (an phríomhphearsa) = 1 mharc”, then “5 phointe eolais ag teastáil (5 mharc an ceann ar an gcéad dhá phointe eolais+ 4 mharc an ceann ar an trí phointe eolais eile)” (22), then title 1 + author 1; its title block prints no “(2 mharc)” of its own.

Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní): (i) prints four questions (a)–(d) at (2 mharc) each, (a)–(c) with “Freagraí samplacha:” and (d) “Úlla + caora finiúna = 1 mharc + 1 mharc”; (ii) is priced “(2 phointe eolais ar 4 mharc an ceann)” and (iii) “(5 mharc ar an gceann is fearr + 4 mharc ar an gceann eile)”. An Spailpín Fánach: (i)(a), (c), (d) at (2 mharc) with sample answers, (b) a list of places “(1 mharc + 1 mharc)”; (ii) “= (4 mharc +4 mharc)”; (iii) “Is maith / Ní maith = (1 mharc) + dhá fháth = (4 mharc + 4 mharc)”. The scheme prints no (8 marc)/(9 marc) of its own for them.

3B(a) prices (i) “An téama a lua = 3 mharc Forbairt ar an téama = 4 mharc”, (ii) “Íomhá / pictiúr a lua = 1 mharc Forbairt = 3 mharc 2 íomhá / phictiúr ar 4 mharc an ceann”, (iii) “Rud amháin a thaitin leat = 4 mharc Rud amháin nár thaitin leat= 4 mharc”; 3B(b) (i) “Lomphointe + Forbairt= 2 phointe ar 4 mharc an ceann = 8 marc”, (ii) “Mothú a lua=1 mharc + dhá fháth :3 mharc + 2 mharc”, (iii) “Is maith / Ní maith = (1 mharc) + dhá fháth = 4 mharc + 4 mharc”. Each 3B title line prints only “(2 mharc)”, no split: the title criterion is 0/2 (coordinator ruling of 5 November 2026 on 2-mark items with no printed 1-mark partial).

3A and 3B each close with an examiner’s instruction (“Nóta: Caithfidh an Scrúdaitheoir an marc don Ábhar … a thaispeáint go soiléir sna hionaid chuí ar an bhfreagarleabhar.”), where to record marks in the answer book; it is on no card.

Scheme misprints kept as printed in the guidance: missing spaces after commas (A 1(a) “an stát,bhí”, “Mheiriceá,ag”, B 1(a) “Dé Domhnaigh ,9 Nollaig 2012”), A 3(a) “earraíd” and “chaighdéan”, B 4(a) “traenail” without its fada and its opening quotation mark, Mo ghrá-sa (i)(d) “caora finiúna” (the poem prints “fíniúna”), An Spailpín Fánach (i)(b) “aonach hireálta”, and the play’s “( 5 mharc=”.
